tasks.title: Lecture #25
tasks.instruction: Listen to a talk in a psychology class.
tasks.transcript:
Professor: The bystander effect is a social psychological theory according to which individuals are less likely to offer help to a victim when other people are present. The theory was first proposed by researchers in the 1960s, based on observations. The bystander effect can be explained through two primary factors: diffusion of responsibility and social influence. Diffusion of responsibility occurs when people believe that someone else will take action, and so they feel less personal responsibility. Social influence involves looking to others for cues on how to behave, especially in ambiguous situations. If others are not helping, individuals may interpret the situation as non-emergency and refrain from intervening.
More recent studies, however, have disputed the claim that the presence of more bystanders can decrease the likelihood of assistance. One study from 2019 that analyzed video footage from multiple cities found that in 9 out of 10 incidents, at least one bystander did take action to help. This study found that a bystander was actually more likely to intervene when more bystanders were present. Some factors that may influence bystander behavior include the level of danger and whether bystanders know each other.

questions.stem: What is the main topic of the talk?

options.A: How a social psychological theory was developed
options.B: How the presence of others can affect a decision
options.C: How to help people in different emergencies
options.D: How to help people in different emergencies

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：这段讲话的主题是什么？ 定位原文： The bystander effect is a social psychological theory according to which individuals are less likely to offer help to a victim when other people are present. ... The bystander effect can be explained through two primary factors: diffusion of responsibility and social influence. ... More recent studies, however, have disputed the claim that the presence of more bystanders can decrease the likelihood of assistance. 选项分析： A. How a social psychological theory was developed（一种社会心理学理论是如何发展的）。讲话提到理论提出于20世纪60年代，但未详细阐述其发展过程，所以A选项错误。 B. How the presence of others can affect a decision（他人的存在如何影响一个人的决定）。讲话围绕旁观者效应展开，核心讨论他人的存在如何影响个体是否提供帮助的决定，因此B选项正确。 C. How to help people in different emergencies（如何在不同紧急情况下帮助他人）。讲话未提供具体的帮助方法，所以C选项错误。 D. How to identify emergency situations（如何识别紧急情况）。讲话虽提到在模糊情境中人们会观察他人行为来判断是否为紧急情况，但这并非主题，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: According to the talk, how might social influence affect an individual's behavior?

options.A: A person may interpret a situation as less urgent if no one around them intervenes.
options.B: A person may be unwilling to be the first to act.
options.C: An individual is more likely to act to impress the others in the group.
options.D: An individual is less likely to act when specifically asked to do so.

questions.analysis: 答案：A 题目问的是：根据讲话，社会影响如何影响个体的行为？ 定位原文： Social influence involves looking to others for cues on how to behave, especially in ambiguous situations. If others are not helping, individuals may interpret the situation as non-emergency and refrain from intervening. 选项分析： A. A person may interpret a situation as less urgent if no one around them intervenes（如果周围没有人介入，一个人可能会将情况解读为不那么紧急）。讲话明确指出在模糊情境中，如果他人不帮忙，个体可能将其视为非紧急情况而不干预，因此A选项正确。 B. A person may be unwilling to be the first to act（一个人可能不愿意第一个采取行动）。讲话未提及“第一个行动”的意愿问题，所以B选项错误。 C. An individual is more likely to act to impress the others in the group（个体更有可能为了给群体中其他人留下印象而采取行动）。基于讲话未提及给他人留下印象的动机，所以C选项错误。 D. An individual is less likely to act when specifically asked to do so（当被明确要求采取行动时，个体更不可能行动）。讲话未讨论被明确要求的情况，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: Why does the speaker discuss a study from 2019?

options.A: To illustrate how new technologies have improved social psychological research
options.B: To provide evidence that challenges earlier research
options.C: To support the idea that it is dangerous for bystanders to offer help
options.D: To argue that not many bystanders are willing to help

questions.analysis: 答案：B 题目问的是：演讲者为什么讨论2019年的一项研究？ 定位原文： More recent studies, however, have disputed the claim that the presence of more bystanders can decrease the likelihood of assistance. One study from 2019 that analyzed video footage from multiple cities found that in 9 out of 10 incidents, at least one bystander did take action to help. This study found that a bystander was actually more likely to intervene when more bystanders were present. 选项分析： A. To illustrate how new technologies have improved social psychological research（为了说明新技术如何改进了社会心理学研究）。讲话提到研究分析了视频录像，但并未强调新技术的作用，所以A选项错误。 B. To provide evidence that challenges earlier research（为了提供挑战早期研究的证据）。讲话明确指出近年来的研究对“更多旁观者会降低帮助可能性”这一观点提出了质疑，并用2019年的研究作为证据，因此B选项正确。 C. To support the idea that it is dangerous for bystanders to offer help（为了支持旁观者提供帮助是危险的观点）。讲话未提及帮助的危险性，所以C选项错误。 D. To argue that not many bystanders are willing to help（为了论证没有多少旁观者愿意提供帮助）。研究发现9/10的事件中至少有一名旁观者采取了行动，表明大多数情况下有人愿意帮助，所以D选项错误。

questions.stem: What is NOT mentioned as a factor that influences bystander behavior?

options.D: The familiarity of bystanders to one another

questions.analysis: 答案：C 题目问的是：哪个选项没有被提及作为影响旁观者行为的因素？ 定位原文： Some factors that may influence bystander behavior include the level of danger and whether bystanders know each other. 选项分析： A. The number of bystanders（旁观者的数量）。讲话前半部分讨论旁观者效应的经典理论涉及旁观者数量，后半部分的2019年研究也讨论了更多旁观者时干预的可能性，所以A选项被提及。 B. The degree of danger（危险程度）。讲话明确指出“危险程度”是影响旁观者行为的因素之一，所以B选项被提及。 C. The location of the incident（事件发生的地点）。讲话全文未提及地点因素，因此C选项未被提及，符合题意。 D. The familiarity of bystanders to one another（旁观者之间的熟悉程度）。讲话明确指出“旁观者是否互相认识”是影响因素之一，所以D选项被提及。
